Auction grades

You are wiring money against a grade. So we publish the sheet.

Every unit carries the auction inspector's own sheet — grade, condition notes and diagram — not our summary of it. The scale is the Japanese auction standard, including repaired units, which we never list as anything else.

  • 5 Effectively as new — negligible wear, no repair history.
  • 4.5 Excellent condition with only minor cosmetic marks.
  • 4 Good condition, normal use marks, mechanically sound.
  • 3.5 Visible wear or small panel damage noted on the sheet.
  • 3 Older or higher-use unit, condition notes worth reading closely.
  • R Repaired — accident history disclosed on the sheet.
  • RA Repaired, light — minor recorded repair work.
  • ✓ Real auction sheet published with every listing — grade, inspector notes, diagram.
  • ✓ Repair/accident history (修復歴) disclosed, not implied.
  • ✓ Odometer photographed at the time of listing.
  • ✓ Licensed secondhand dealer — verify our registration any time.
  • ✓ Chassis number cross-checked against the original Japanese registration, on request.

Process

How buying works

The same six steps, every time — no surprises mid-purchase.

  1. 01

    Browse or request sourcing

    Pick a unit in stock, or tell us what you need at auction.

  2. 02

    Check the auction sheet

    Real grade, condition notes and photos before you commit.

  3. 03

    Request a quote

    FOB, C&F or CIF, priced to your destination port.

  4. 04

    Invoice & payment

    Bank wire, confirmed before anything ships.

  5. 05

    Shipping arranged

    RoRo or container booking from Yokohama or Nagoya.

  6. 06

    Customs & delivery

    Export certificate, B/L and invoice sent to you.

Sourcing request

Can't find the right vehicle?

Tell us the unit, the budget and the port. If it isn't already in stock we bid for it at auction, send you the sheet before committing, and cross-check the chassis number against the original Japanese registration.
